assertions: Comparison preserves native identity, absent-pointer, WhichId, concrete type and virtual payload order.
Wrong-type payload comparators cannot hide item-set inequality or suppress actual replacement.

stackDivergence.rationale: Task148 restores SfxPoolItem.areSame identity/absent-pointer/WhichId/exact-concrete-type/payload comparison order and adopts it in original SfxItemSet Equals and Put sites. Concrete JS class identity represents the native per-derived-class ItemType identity; numeric C++ enum/ABI values are not materialized. Both host null and undefined represent absent pointers. Direct payload equals retains its subclass contract; the shared helper owns the extra identity and type guards. Real value/sentinel and item-set replacement regressions use permissive comparison spies to prove that wrong-type payload equality is never invoked. Shared Writer consumers use the same corrected owners. JS GC owns lifetime; no native interning/refcount/weak/holder manager, type-number ABI or fake EditTextObject is introduced. This is a prerequisite for actual rich-text paragraph/character attribute comparison; EditTextObject/ScPageHFItem and full Calc pool/document/connected UI/same-model ODS remain pending. UI localization stays deferred. Existing semantic statuses and deliberate I/O/recovery deviations remain unchanged.
